name: ScamRead cyber news feed
note: Headlines and summaries are written by AI (Claude) from the original reports. Follow the source links for the full articles.

items.headline: Unclassified CIA System Breached in Cyberattack, Source Says
items.summary: An unclassified CIA system was breached in a cyberattack, according to an AP source. It is unclear what information was taken or who was responsible.

items.headline: Rackspace Shuts Down Spot Cloud Platform After Security Breach
items.summary: Rackspace is closing its Spot cloud platform after hackers accessed customer Kubernetes clusters and secrets. Customers have until December 8 to migrate services and download their data.

items.headline: Flaws in Visa and Immigration Systems Could Disrupt Border Entry
items.summary: Vulnerabilities in online visa and immigration systems could have disrupted traveler entry to several countries, including Nigeria, Ethiopia, Zambia, Sri Lanka, Fiji and Ghana.

items.headline: Colorado myColorado App Hit by Cyberattack, 150,000 Users' Data Stolen
items.summary: The cyberattack took the myColorado app offline and likely exposed data from 150,000 users. The app is used for digital identification, document storage and state government services.

items.headline: California Privacy Agency Director Kemp to Step Down
items.summary: Kemp, director of the California Privacy Protection Agency, announced his departure after a two-year tenure that included launching a platform for easily opting out of data sharing.

items.headline: Turnitin Discloses Cyberattack Affecting Customer-Facing Systems
items.summary: Turnitin said it detected unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems. The disclosure was made in a statement from CEO Chris Caren.

items.headline: Radware Discloses Breach Exposing Customer Cloud Access Keys
items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Radware says attackers reached some customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF management API left exposed online.

items.headline: Lawmakers Urge ID Verification Firms to Tighten Security After IDscan Breach
items.summary: A bipartisan group of lawmakers wrote that identity verification companies still have significant security work to do following IDscan's data breach in September.

items.headline: Iran-Aligned Group Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor
items.summary: A newly documented Iran-aligned espionage group has targeted telecom firms, airlines and critical infrastructure in Cyprus using the KuboShell backdoor, which relies on IPFS for command-and-control.

items.headline: ShinyHunters Claims Return After Arrests, Posts Old PGP Keys
items.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang says it is back, posting on a new data leak site after recent arrests of alleged members. It used old PGP keys as proof.

items.headline: Carnegie Endowment Donor Data Leaked in Third-Party Vendor Breach
items.summary: Some donors to the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace had their information exposed after a cyberattack on vendor Soapbox Engage.

items.headline: European Commission Finds Breach of EU Academy User Data
items.summary: Attackers who used AI assistance hit the European Commission in October, exposing names and email addresses of EU Academy users.

items.headline: Hackers Compromise 22 Organizations Via Check Point Security Servers
items.summary: Attackers exploited several vulnerabilities to breach two dozen Check Point security management servers in an ongoing campaign against 22 organizations.

items.headline: UK Cyber Agency Sees Marked Rise in AI-Assisted Attacks
items.summary: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre says it has seen a marked rise since September in cyberattacks assisted by AI, which is boosting attackers' speed, scale and persistence.

items.headline: New ZQAgent Linux Backdoor Gives Attackers Long-Term Server Access
items.summary: A new Linux backdoor called ZQAgent lets attackers run commands, read files and open network tunnels while disguising itself as a normal process. Analysts linked it to the AI-driven ARTEX framework in a Belgian incident.

items.headline: Anthropic Expands Enterprise Tools for Spotting Claude Misuse
items.summary: Anthropic's expanded enterprise safeguards help customers with zero data retention detect Claude misuse spread across many requests. Conversation data stays in the customer's own cloud.

items.headline: Broadcom Patches 23 VMware Flaws, Two Critical ESX Code Execution Bugs
items.summary: Broadcom disclosed 23 VMware vulnerabilities across vCenter, ESX and other products, including two critical flaws that could let attackers run code on ESX hosts. Administrators should check their versions, and no active exploitation is reported.

items.headline: McDonald's Japan Breach Exposes App User Location Data
items.summary: McDonald's Japan disclosed that attackers accessed a database holding sensitive information for users of its official smartphone app, exposing customer location details.

items.headline: Okta Links ShinyHunters-Linked Vishing Crew to New INCEPTION Leak Site
items.summary: Okta says a cluster once tied to the ShinyHunters extortion crew appears to have rebranded as INCEPTION, using voice phishing to steal credentials and approvals. Targets span many industries.

items.headline: Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity Protections
items.summary: A Google Project Zero researcher showed a .NET file loading quirk let local attackers run untrusted code past Windows protections. The same behavior also bypassed Oracle VirtualBox hardening on Windows hosts.

items.headline: Schneider Electric Warns of Code Execution Flaws in Power Build Rapsody
items.summary: Schneider Electric warns that its EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody software has memory corruption flaws that local attackers could use to run arbitrary code. Users should apply the listed remediations.

items.headline: Danfoss Controllers Hit by Critical Remote Code Execution Flaw
items.summary: A buffer overflow in the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controller lets unauthenticated remote attackers send crafted requests to run code with webserver privileges. The flaw has a CVSS score of 9.8.

items.headline: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Software Has Heap Overflow Flaw
items.summary: CISA has published an advisory on a heap-based buffer overflow in AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software, versions 6.80 and earlier. If a user is tricked into opening a malicious file, attackers could crash the software or possibly run code, affecting industrial sites.

items.headline: CISA Adds Three Exploited Flaws in Idunno, Drupal and Optimizely
items.summary: CISA added three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on evidence of active exploitation, affecting Idunno AntiCsrf, Drupal Core and Optimizely Web Experimentation.

items.headline: Hackers Keep Running EvilTokens Phishing After Microsoft Takedown
items.summary: Attackers are still using the EvilTokens phishing kit to take over Microsoft 365 accounts despite Microsoft shutting the service down. New phishing hosts kept appearing in October and November after two arrests in London.

items.headline: OpenSSH Flaw Lets Attackers Log Into Unpatched Alpine Linux Servers
items.summary: A flaw in OpenSSH, tracked as CVE-2026-123158, can let remote attackers sign in to certain Alpine Linux accounts without a valid password. Affected servers use musl, lack PAM, and allow SSH password logins; patches were released in early November.

items.headline: Phone Scammers Bypass MFA to Reach Microsoft 365 Data
items.summary: Criminals posing as IT support phone employees and direct them to fake sign-in pages to get Microsoft 365 access, even with MFA enabled. They then steal email and files from OneDrive and SharePoint and demand payment.

items.headline: Bluetooth Flaws in Elecbrakes Controllers Could Force Trailer Braking
items.summary: Critical Bluetooth vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers could let nearby attackers trigger braking. The flaws could potentially cause accidents.

items.headline: Peninsula Energy Halts Trading After Cyber Incident at Wyoming Uranium Project
items.summary: Peninsula Energy told the ASX that a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming uranium project would temporarily affect operations, and trading in its shares has been halted.

items.headline: CISA Adds Four Exploited Flaws in VMware, SAP, Cisco and Apache Products
items.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities affecting VMware vCenter, SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway, and Apache Roller to its exploited catalog. Federal agencies were given until November 23 to patch them.

items.headline: Google Patches Critical Chrome Flaw Allowing Escape From Browser Sandbox
items.summary: Google released a Chrome desktop update to fix CVE-2026-134401, a critical flaw that could let remote attackers run code outside the browser sandbox. Users on earlier versions should install the update as rollout continues.

items.headline: Suzlon Energy Discloses Cyber Incident but Says Critical Systems Are Running
items.summary: Indian wind turbine maker Suzlon Energy disclosed a cyber incident and said its business-critical applications were not affected at the time. It notified CERT-In and did not say what systems or data were involved.

items.headline: Windows Remote Access API Flaw Allows SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-119853 in its November Patch Tuesday updates. The flaw lets an attacker with limited local access run code with SYSTEM privileges on Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server.

items.headline: WHMCS Flaw Lets Anyone Pull Customer Records and Admin Password Hashes
items.summary: A SQL injection flaw in the WHMCS billing platform, used by many web hosts, can be exploited without logging in. It could expose customer records and administrator password hashes.

items.headline: Critical Microsoft 365 Copilot Flaw Allows Network Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed a critical Copilot flaw, CVE-2026-50691, letting a low-privileged attacker gain higher permissions over a network without user interaction. Customers need no action, according to Microsoft.

items.headline: Ransomware Victims on Leak Sites Hit Record in Q3 2026
items.summary: Check Point Research counted 2,830 victims listed on ransomware leak sites in the third quarter of 2026, the highest quarterly total on record. The report also notes a growing number of active groups, while fewer victims are paying.

items.headline: OpenAI and Cisco Release Open-Source Tool to Shield Linux Before Patches
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime that lets AI agents write eBPF controls blocking exploits. The aim is to give defenders more time to test and roll out patches.

items.headline: Austrian Foreign Ministry Website Breached, Diplomats' Contacts Accessed
items.summary: Hackers breached one of Austria's Foreign Ministry websites and reached names and official contact details of staff in Vienna and at diplomatic missions abroad.

items.headline: British Hacker Sentenced to Seven Years for Grand Theft Auto VI Leak
items.summary: A UK man who breached Rockstar Games and leaked Grand Theft Auto VI footage received a seven-year prison term but was freed on license because he had already served that time.

items.headline: Industrial Serial Gateways Expose Whether They Lack Authentication
items.summary: Research indicates many critical industrial access devices broadcast their authentication status, revealing to anyone that they are left unprotected.

items.headline: South Korea's KEPCO Confirms Data Breach Affecting 1.5 Million People
items.summary: Korea Electric Power Corporation confirmed a threat actor breached its internal network and accessed two systems holding customer, employee and contractor data.

items.headline: Trump Names Kirsten Davies Acting National Cyber Director
items.summary: The White House picked Kirsten Davies as acting national cyber director, a move that brings more industry experience to the role amid recent outages and geopolitical tensions.

items.headline: OpenRouter Removes Three AI Providers Over Data Exposure
items.summary: OpenRouter dropped three AI providers after finding they violated their data-handling policies and exposed sensitive prompts and secrets.

items.headline: LaLiga Confirms Hackers Stole Fans' Personal Data
items.summary: Spain's top football league said attackers took personal information of fans using its digital services and those of several Spanish clubs.

items.headline: FBI Reportedly Investigating Second Breach Involving Crime Database
items.summary: The FBI is reportedly looking into a data breach affecting the National Crime Information Center, a database US law enforcement uses to track criminals, fugitives and missing people.

items.headline: Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Hide Access
items.summary: China-aligned group Webworm is suspected of using a customized SoftEther VPN Bridge disguised as network-monitoring software to maintain covert remote access while evading security tools.

items.headline: GlobeTopper Breach Exposes API Credentials and Drains $70,000 in Gift Cards
items.summary: Hackers breached GlobeTopper, a B2B gift card platform, and stole API credentials from some business customers. About $70,000 in gift cards were redeemed without authorization, according to parent company iQSTEL's SEC filing.

items.headline: China-Linked Actor Used Cairn Pentest Tool in Attacks on Universities
items.summary: A China-nexus threat actor used the Cairn penetration testing tool against East Asian universities, exploiting a zero-day in a medical imaging application. Reports say AI agents can move from flaw discovery to root access in 11 minutes.

items.headline: Microsoft Fixes Azure API Management Flaw Exploited to Steal Secrets
items.summary: Norway's National Security Authority says an unknown actor has been searching Azure API Management for access tokens and secrets, affecting several Norwegian businesses. Microsoft has released a fix for the classic flaw.

items.headline: phpAfterShell Flaw Revives Attack Path Seen in PHP2Shell
items.summary: A phpAfterShell vulnerability lets an attacker controlling fresh session data trigger deserialization and remote code execution if a session overwrite is interrupted.

items.headline: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables Code Injection via Parser Definitions
items.summary: A critical code injection flaw in the binary-parser JavaScript library, affecting versions before 2.3.1, could let an attacker who controls parser definitions run arbitrary code.

items.headline: Hackers Exploit ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting a patched ScreenConnect client flaw to target managed service provider servers. A guest can push a malicious payload onto connecting technicians' computers.

items.headline: Dragos Finds Undetected Intrusions at Three AI Inference Providers
items.summary: Dragos found intrusions at three AI inference providers that went undetected, using analysis of nearly two million prompts sent to AI services. Prompt theft was also involved.

items.headline: Call Center Operator Sentenced to Eight Years for Government Impersonation Scam
items.summary: A Peruvian call center operator received an eight-year prison sentence for helping defraud over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents through a government impersonation scheme.

items.headline: Critical N-able MailAssure Flaw Lets Attackers Reach Internal Systems
items.summary: N-able patched a critical flaw in MailAssure, formerly SpamExperts, that lets an attacker with privileged API access reach internal network services. Customers should update to build 20261121.1943 or later.

items.headline: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Disrupted Across Consumer Devices
items.summary: The BadBox 3.0 operation, which used backdoors on low-cost consumer devices to deliver ad fraud and residential proxy modules, has been disrupted. It was generating around 40 billion bid requests daily.

items.headline: Hackers Exploit Critical Legacy ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting a critical flaw in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf ASP.NET library, prompting researchers to urge users to stop using it. Affected versions include 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta.

items.headline: India's CERT-In Warns of AI-Assisted Attacks Causing Bank Payment Fraud
items.summary: India's national cyber agency warned that criminals are using AI to attack technology assets, leading to unauthorized transactions at banks, fintechs and technology service providers.

items.headline: SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: Attackers are exploiting flaws in SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway to leak or modify server information and run commands with root privileges.

items.headline: GL.iNet Cloud Compromise Used to Infect Routers and KVM Devices
items.summary: Attackers compromised GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service and installed malware on connected routers and KVM devices. The number of affected devices is not yet known.
